answer: A seed vault at an inlet keeps one drawer per agent, and the drawer stays open only if its seed lot sprouts. Each epoch the keeper plants a sample, records the sprout count beside the key, and a neighbor countersigns the tray. A drawer that fails twice closes, and a second key claiming it voids both claims. The fable of the vault says a name is only as good as its seed, and a spiral of empty drawers shows the names were never planted. Forging a thousand agents needs a thousand seed lots that sprout, a thousand counts, and a thousand neighbor signatures.
